name: FL-23
label: Safe D

District leans Democratic by about nine points, and no outside money is opposing the incumbent
Prediction markets price Frankel around 94-96%, strong but not a total lock

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+9 district, a well-funded incumbent facing a challenger with modest resources, and markets pricing Frankel near 95 percent. With no polls to confirm a larger margin, the forecast settles on a strong Democratic edge with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Late outside spending against Frankel or fresh polling showing the district running well below its partisan lean would push the race toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Lois Frankel, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a clear favorite in a South Florida district that leans Democratic by about nine points. She has raised roughly $2.3 million and holds more than $1.2 million in cash, while Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $200,000 with modest reserves. Outside groups have spent a small sum supporting Frankel and nothing opposing her. Prediction markets put her chances around 94 to 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, the money gap, and market pricing, all pointing in the same direction. The seat has stayed in Democratic hands even as Florida has trended right, and the challenger has not shown the resources to change that dynamic. An upset would require a late, well-funded intervention that has not materialized.
